## Findings
- claim-1: Original Conjecture 4.10 states that both Theorem 4.8 families are minimal: the right-adjoined family \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}\) and the lower-adjoined family \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\), for \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\). [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 864-876] [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 938-946]
- claim-2: The 2024 paper’s Theorem 1.2 proves minimality only for the lower-adjoined family \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\), for bigrassmannian \(v_{r,s,t,n}\), in \(H^*(\mathrm{Gr}_{r,n})\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 219-235]
- claim-3: Its Corollary 4.6 again concludes minimality only for that lower-adjoined family. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 827-832]
- claim-4: The right-adjoined family is addressed only in Remark 4.7: it is identified as the conjugate family, and the paper says one “could straightforwardly” transpose the arguments to prove its minimality; no transposed theorem or corollary is stated there. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 833-840]
## Strategy
Compare the two distinct inspected works. RWY (2011) states Conjecture 4.10: both Theorem 4.8 families are minimal [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 938-946]. St. Dizier–Yong (2024) broadly says “We prove the minimality conjecture” [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 124-130] and identifies that as its goal [lines 180-181], but its formal Theorem 1.2 and Corollary 4.6 establish only the lower-adjoined family [lines 219-235; 827-832]. Remark 4.7 describes the right-adjoined family and says one “could” transpose the arguments to prove it [lines 833-840].

Thus the precise source-relative reconciliation is: the 2024 paper globally claims resolution of Conjecture 4.10, while its explicit theorem/corollary text proves only one clause and leaves the other as a proposed transposition. This bibliographic classification is separate from the accepted project proof of both families.

## Gaps
No gap in this bounded reconciliation. The search record contains two distinct works: RWY (2011) and the 2024 St. Dizier–Yong work; arXiv 2209.02011 and the DOI record are versions of the latter. No additional inspected source supplies a separately stated theorem for the right-adjoined clause.
